name: Kharonoi
body:
Kharonoi
CR 4

This gaunt humanoid is shrouded in a hooded black robe, parched skin making its faunt face seem almost a skull and its hands nearly skeletal.

XP 1,200
N Medium outsider (psychopomp)
Init +5; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, spiritsense; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 17, touch 15, flat-footed 12 (+5 Dex, +2 natural)
hp 52 (7d10+14)
Fort +8, Ref +7, Will +8
DR 5/adamantine; Immune death effects, disease, poison; Resist cold 10, electricity 10

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 30 ft. (average)
Melee quarterstaff +10/+5 (1d6+4)
Special Attacks spirit touch

STATISTICS

Str 17, Dex 21, Con 14, Int 10, Wis 14, Cha 13
Base Atk +7; CMB +10; CMD 25
Feats Furious Focus, Power Attack, Pushing Assault, Vital Strike
Skills Intimidate +10, Knowledge (planes) +10, Knowledge (religion) +10, Perception +10, Profession (sailor) +10, Stealth +15, Swim +10
Languages Abyssal, Celestial, Common, Infernal
SQ unsinkable Gear quarterstaff

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Unsinkable (Su)

While the kharonoi is in its boat, it can automatically control the boat’s direction and speed, and the boat can’t sink or capsize. The kharonoi is immune to spells and effects that cause it to leave its boat.

ECOLOGY

Environment River Styx
Organization solitary or raft (2-5)
Treasure none

The legendary Charon is famed as ferryman of the dead, carrying spirits across the Styx if they were buried or cremated with a coin in their mouth, leaving them to wander the banks forever if they don’t. However, Charon himself does not deign to pick up the dead from every world at all times, instead dispatching an armada of minions to cross the planar divide as psychopomps, leading the spirits of the dead to their final rest. These servants are the kharonoi, servants of the cult of Charon gifted with a kind of twisted immortality, though bound to serve as deathless ferrymen.

They appear as ugly older men with a grim faces and crooked noses, often with a beard and conical hat. They await lost spirits to take payment for their crossing into the afterlife, and if confronted with violence they may try to knock their passengers into the eerie waters of the Styx or may simply abandon their skiffs and fly away leaving their companions adrift until the eddies of the mystic river bring them to the bank hours later. Those thus forsaken must find their own way back to the land of the living.
